item.title: Spex Glance 0.3.0
item.description:
Spex Glance 0.3.0

Four sections, four shortcuts

The window is now split into Positions, Orders, Settled and P&L. Press ⌘1 to ⌘4 to jump between them, or ⌘⇧[ and ⌘⇧] to cycle. The money tiles and the status line stay put above all four.

  • **Positions** is the view you know. Nothing changed there.
  • **Orders** holds your resting orders, moved out from under the positions list into their own section. It still only shows them — Spex Glance never places, changes or cancels an order.
  • **Settled** lists every sports market Kalshi has settled for you, newest first, grouped by day with the day's net. Each row shows Won or Lost, what it made or lost, and the fee. A sport filter and a fees checkbox sit at the top.
  • **P&L** charts it. The realized line is rebuilt from Kalshi's own settlement records every time you open the app, so it's correct from the first launch and nothing is stored for it. Pick 1D, 7D, 30D or All; untick "Include fees" to see gross.

Work Mode hides the P&L section entirely and drops the dollar signs from Orders and Settled.

Live Line (optional)

Kalshi has no history of what your portfolio was worth over time, so if you want that line, the app has to record it. Live Line is off until you turn it on in Settings → Charts.

  • When it's on, the app samples your sports total about once a minute while prices move and draws it on the P&L section.
  • Turning it on asks where to keep the history. **This Mac only** keeps it encrypted inside the app on this computer; it exists nowhere else, and Disconnect erases it. **iCloud** also syncs it between your Macs through your private iCloud storage, which Apple encrypts. If iCloud isn't available, the history stays on this Mac and syncs once it is.
  • Your Kalshi key is never part of what's stored or synced.
  • "Save as CSV…" on the card exports every sample.
  • The history is kept at full detail for a day, then thinned to one point per five minutes for a week and one per hour after that.

Your settings now actually stick

A bug in every earlier version meant the app's settings — Work Mode, sport filter, sort order, menu bar choices — quietly reset whenever the app relaunched. Fixed. Because of the same fix, this update moves the app to a new identity under the hood, and two things need a one-time redo:

  • **Launch at login** will show as off. Turn it back on in Settings → Menu bar if you had it.
  • **The widget** needs to be removed and added again in Notification Center.

Your Kalshi key carries over on its own; you won't need to reconnect.

Under the hood

  • Settled markets come from Kalshi's settlements endpoint, pulled incrementally after the first load.
  • Live Line iCloud sync uses CloudKit's private database directly: one record per Mac per hour, so two Macs never conflict.
  • App Group and keychain group are now `<TeamID>.bet.spex.glance`; the old `com.example` ones are read once to migrate and will be dropped in the next release.

item.title: Spex Glance 0.2.2
item.description:
Spex Glance 0.2.2

Know when it's your network, not Kalshi

  • If your Mac loses its network connection, the line at the top of the window now says "Computer network offline" (with when the numbers were last updated) instead of quietly going stale.
  • The menu bar icon turns gray with an "offline" badge, and the dropdown says the same. It clears on its own when the connection comes back.
  • Before this, a dropped Wi-Fi connection could show up as "Kalshi down", which wasn't fair to Kalshi. The app now checks your own connection first and only reports on Kalshi when it can actually reach it.
  • When the connection returns, the app reconnects and refreshes on its own within a few seconds; you don't have to wait for the next scheduled refresh or hit Refresh yourself.

item.title: Spex Glance 0.2.1
item.description:
Spex Glance 0.2.1

A small follow-up to 0.2.0. Everyone on 0.2.0 should take this one.

Fixes

  • 0.2.0 reported itself as version 1.0 in About and in update checks, which made the app keep offering the 0.2.0 update to itself. Fixed; this build and every one after it carries the right version.
  • The Work Mode shortcut is now ⌘⇧M. Plain ⌘M is macOS's own Minimize shortcut and won that fight. The Positions menu shows the new key.

New

  • A small "Kalshi Health" dot next to "Live" at the top of the window shows Kalshi's own status at all times: green when Kalshi reports itself up, ember when degraded, red when down, gray during maintenance. Hover it for the reason. Before, this only appeared when something was wrong, so a healthy Kalshi and a check that wasn't running looked the same.

item.title: Spex Glance 0.2.0
item.description:
Spex Glance 0.2.0

Your positions now update the moment they change

Until now, prices streamed live but everything else waited for a refresh every five minutes. This version listens to Kalshi for the rest too.

  • A fill, a sale, or a new order shows up in the window, the menu bar, and the widget within a couple of seconds.
  • When Kalshi decides a game, "Final · awaiting settlement" flips to Won or Lost right away instead of on the next refresh. Combo legs get their check or cross the same way.
  • Paid-out positions leave the list on their own, and your Cash figure catches up a moment later.
  • The five-minute refresh still runs in the background as a safety net, so a dropped connection never leaves stale numbers on screen.

Know how fresh the numbers are

  • Kalshi stamps every message with the time it left their servers. Spex Glance now compares that to the time it arrives.
  • The dot next to "live" turns amber and shows how many seconds behind you are if the feed falls more than 15 seconds back. Green means you're current.
  • "Updated" in the window and the time on the widget now reflect the last live change, not just the last full refresh.

See when Kalshi itself is having trouble

  • The menu bar icon and P&L turn ember when Kalshi is degraded (trading paused, a shard paused, the feed struggling) and red when it's down. Gray means scheduled maintenance.
  • Open the dropdown for the reason and how long it's been going on. A Status page button opens the community-run kalshistatus.com in your browser.
  • The app asks Kalshi's own status endpoint once a minute. It still contacts nothing but Kalshi.
  • Your last good numbers stay on screen the whole time; nothing is blanked out.

Work Mode, expanded

  • Press ⌘M to toggle Work Mode from anywhere in the app.
  • Work Mode now also hides the Cash, Positions and Total tiles and the buttons at the bottom of the window, so only your positions are on screen when you're sharing it.
  • The "Spex Glance" wordmark no longer sits at the top of the main window.

Small fixes

  • Version numbers now show correctly in About and in update checks.
  • Settings → About has a direct link to report a problem or ask a question (a GitHub issue, with your app and macOS versions filled in).
  • Automatic update checks are on by default; no first-launch question. You can turn them off in Settings → Updates.

Under the hood

  • One WebSocket connection to Kalshi carries prices, position changes, order changes and market results. The app still only ever subscribes; it cannot place, change or cancel anything.
  • Uses the same free, read-only API key as before. Nothing to set up.
